advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Terminate the child pytest process (or its process group) in the SIGINT/SIGTERM cleanup handler before removing the run_dir and exiting.
evidence: scripts/run_default_tests.py:175: `shutil.rmtree(run_dir, ignore_errors=True)` then `raise SystemExit(128 + signum)` with no propagation to the pytest child
scripts/run_default_tests.py:218: `return subprocess.run([..."pytest"...], check=False).returncode` — the child is not stored or killed on signal
ABSENCE: no terminate()/kill() of the pytest process in the signal handler, and the registry entry is deleted while its workers may still be alive
advisory.finding: On SIGINT/SIGTERM the cleanup handler removes the run_dir and raises SystemExit but never terminates the child `pytest` subprocess spawned by `subprocess.run`; a SIGTERM delivered only to the parent PID (not the whole process group) leaves the pytest xdist workers running and orphaned.
scenarios: Operator or supervisor sends SIGTERM to the runner PID only; pytest workers continue consuming memory but the registry no longer records them

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Make register_run tolerant of an existing run_dir (unique suffix or exist_ok/retry) so a stale/colliding registry dir cannot abort the run.
evidence: scripts/run_default_tests.py:113: `run_dir = registry_root / f"{int(time.time())}-{os.getpid()}"`
scripts/run_default_tests.py:114: `run_dir.mkdir()` (no exist_ok, no try/except)
scripts/run_default_tests.py:200: `prune_stale_runs` only runs when `locked` is true, so a stale collision can persist when the lock is contended
advisory.finding: `register_run` calls `run_dir.mkdir()` without `exist_ok=True`; the directory name is `f"{int(time.time())}-{os.getpid()}"`. If a prior run's stale entry with the same second+reused PID has not yet been pruned (pruning only happens under the registry lock), the mkdir raises an uncaught FileExistsError and aborts the whole `make test` run.
scenarios: PID reuse plus same-second start with a leftover un-pruned registry dir
Two starts of the same PID within one second (rare but possible on fast restart)

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Surface the environmental-fault / rerun-at-PYTEST_WORKERS=1 guidance on a killed/negative-signal pytest exit code (or always), not only when workers were reduced.
evidence: scripts/run_default_tests.py:209: `if workers < requested:` gates the entire OOM/environmental-fault hint
ticket ba95 AC: 'A killed-by-OOM run is distinguishable from a test failure in guidance/output'
advisory.finding: The environmental-fault / OOM guidance is printed only when `workers < requested`; when the guard leaves the requested worker count unchanged (e.g. plenty of RAM at snapshot but a burst OOM during the run) and the run is then OOM-killed, no message tells the operator to reclassify it as environmental and rerun at PYTEST_WORKERS=1, undermining the ticket AC that an OOM kill be distinguishable from a test failure.
scenarios: Guard keeps requested=4 because the memory snapshot looked fine, then a concurrent peer run spikes and the kernel OOM-kills this suite; operator sees only a nonzero pytest exit with no environmental-fault guidance

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Ensure stale-run pruning happens (or the lock is reliably acquirable) even under contention so OOM-killed/crashed entries cannot indefinitely inflate the active-worker count.
evidence: scripts/run_default_tests.py:199: `if locked: prune_stale_runs(registry_root)` — pruning is conditional on the lock
scripts/run_default_tests.py:205: `active_workers=active_worker_count(registry_root) if locked else requested - 1`
scripts/run_default_tests.py:119: cleanup via `atexit.register(...)` which does not run on SIGKILL/OOM kill
advisory.finding: When the registry lock cannot be acquired within wait_seconds, stale-run pruning is skipped and `active_workers` is guessed as `requested - 1`; combined with the fact that OOM-killed runs cannot fire their atexit/signal cleanup (SIGKILL), dead registry entries accumulate and inflate `active_worker_count` for peers until some later run happens to acquire the lock and prune, so healthy runs may be over-throttled to serial.
scenarios: A run is OOM-killed (SIGKILL) leaving its registry dir; subsequent runs that fail to grab the contended lock never prune it and count its workers as active

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that feeds a sample /proc/meminfo (via tmp file / monkeypatched Path) to available_memory_bytes and asserts the parsed byte count.
evidence: scripts/run_default_tests.py:54-76 parse MemAvailable and darwin pages
search of tests for available_memory_bytes shows only kwargs to choose_worker_count and a monkeypatch (test file lines 28,41,54,109) — the real function is never called
The MemAvailable line parse `int(line.split()[1]) * 1024` and the darwin page-summing loop are untested
advisory.finding: available_memory_bytes() and _darwin_available_memory_bytes() are never exercised: tests either pass the memory value as a direct kwarg to choose_worker_count or monkeypatch guard.available_memory_bytes wholesale, so the /proc/meminfo MemAvailable parse and the darwin vm_stat page-summing parse have no coverage.
scenarios: A malformed /proc/meminfo line, missing MemAvailable, or a vm_stat format change would not be caught

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that pre-creates the lock dir and asserts registry_lock yields False within wait_seconds (use a small wait_seconds), and one asserting it yields True and removes the dir.
evidence: scripts/run_default_tests.py:90-108 registry_lock yields `acquired` (True/False) and rmtrees only when acquired
search of tests for `registry_lock` returned (no matches)
The `locked`/not-locked branch in main (scripts/run_default_tests.py:199, 205) depends on this False return but no test covers the contended path
advisory.finding: registry_lock — the 'non-blocking host slot' whose stated purpose is to serialize registry updates without queueing full runs — has no test for its contention/timeout contract: it is never asserted that a second acquirer yields False after wait_seconds when the lock dir already exists, nor that acquisition yields True and cleans up.
scenarios: A change breaking the timeout fallthrough (e.g. never returning False) would deadlock/queue runs undetected

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a test that installs the signal cleanup on a temp run_dir, invokes the registered handler, and asserts the dir is removed and SystemExit(128+signum) is raised.
evidence: scripts/run_default_tests.py:171-183 installs handlers that rmtree run_dir, chain prior handler, raise SystemExit
no test references signal cleanup (test file has no signal import or _install_signal_cleanup reference)
advisory.finding: _install_signal_cleanup is untested: the contract that a SIGINT/SIGTERM removes the run_dir, chains the previous handler, and raises SystemExit(128+signum) has no coverage.
scenarios: A killed run would leave a stale registry entry (inflating active_worker_count for peers) if cleanup regresses

dropped.checklist_item: - [ ] Add a choose_worker_count test asserting the full requested count is returned when memory/cpu/active_workers are all ample (e.g. requested=4, 64GiB, cpu=8, active=0 -> 4).
evidence: All three choose_worker_count tests assert `workers == 1` (lines 33, 46, 59)

Named violating input with no test: `choose_worker_count(requested=4, available_memory_bytes=64*1024**3, cpu_count=8, active_workers=0)` should return 4 (host_budget=8, remaining_budget=8, min(4,8)=4) but no assertion covers a return value other than 1
scripts/run_default_tests.py:41 `return max(1, min(requested, remaining_budget))` — the min/passthrough arm is never asserted
dropped.finding: choose_worker_count has no test for the unconstrained pass-through case: all three tests assert the result is 1, so a regression that always reduces the count to 1 (e.g. inverting a min/max) would keep every test green while breaking the primary behavior of honoring the requested worker count when the host is idle.
scenarios: A refactor or bug that clamps workers to 1 unconditionally ships undetected because every test expects 1
